title: In R[z]/(z^p-f) in characteristic p, p-th powers lie in R and each prime of R has exactly one prime over it
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number and $R$ an integral domain with $p=0$ in $R$. Let $f\in R$ and let $C=R[z]/(z^p-f)$ be the quotient of the polynomial ring $R[z]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] by the ideal generated by $z^p-f$; assume that $C$ is an integral domain. Then: (1) the ring map $R\to C$ is injective and $C$ is integral over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]; (2) for every $c\in C$ the element $c^p$ lies in the image of $R$; (3) for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$ there is exactly one prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset C$ whose inverse image in $R$ is $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PR (lemma-helper-G-ring, line 12306), proof: 'for every element of B or C some power of it lies in A. Hence there is a unique prime ... lying over p', for the step B subset C = B[z]/(z^p-f); clause (3) from (1), (2) is Algebra, Lemma Tag 0BR8 (lemma-powers, algebra.tex line 10718) with the lying-over Lemma Tag 00GQ (lemma-integral-overring-surjective) used in its proof

proof.text: Set g = X^p - C f. It is monic by Polynomial.monic_X_pow_sub_C and has nonzero degree by Polynomial.degree_X_pow_sub_C since p is prime. AdjoinRoot.of.injective_of_degree_ne_zero gives injectivity. Polynomial.Monic.finite_adjoinRoot supplies a finite R-module, and Algebra.IsIntegral.of_finite proves every quotient element integral over R.

Install characteristic-p instances using CharP.charP_iff_prime_eq_zero in R and AdjoinRoot g. Represent each quotient element by a polynomial (AdjoinRoot.induction_on), and use Polynomial.induction_on' to reduce to sums and monomials. Sums are handled by add_pow_char. For a*z^n, the witness in R is a^p*f^n: AdjoinRoot.eval₂_root gives z^p = of g f and commutativity of natural-number multiplication rewrites (z^n)^p = (z^p)^n. This proves the p-th-power image assertion.

Apply PrimeSpectrum.isHomeomorph_comap (Stacks 0BR8) with exponent p for every element. Positivity follows from hp.pos, and the kernel is zero by RingHom.injective_iff_ker_eq_bot and the injectivity already proved, hence contained in the nilradical. Surjectivity gives a prime above each P; injectivity gives uniqueness, converting between spectrum points and ideals by PrimeSpectrum.ext and congrArg asIdeal.

split_report.summary: Statement kept (checked against 07PR and 0BR8). Five steps: (1) C free on 1,...,z^{p-1} by lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free, so R -> C injective and C finite hence integral (lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral); (2) Frobenius additivity in characteristic p written out (p | binom(p,k) for 0<k<p); (3) c^p = sum b_i^p f^i in the image of R; (4) uniqueness of the prime over p by the argument of the proof of 0BR8 (c in q => c^p in p => c in q'), written in the step; (5) existence by lying over, citing the existing node pqf-lem-lying-over (unit sk-prop-av-pqf-finite, already accepted as a tool use in sk-thm-p1 for lem-weil-pbc-integral-cover-trivial-cohomology). No new node. The hypotheses that R and C are domains are not used by the proof (clauses (1)-(3) hold for any ring R with p=0); the statement is kept since the citer has them.
